queries.name: catalog
queries.description: Browse everything on offer. The whole catalogue comes back in one call, so this is the cheap way to see what exists before narrowing.

output_schema.description: Every item on offer, one row each. Not paginated.

sku.description: Stable item handle -- reference items by this, never by a numeric id.

queries.name: search_hotels
queries.description: Find hotels matching what the human actually asked for; narrow with the filters this verb declares rather than pulling the whole catalogue. A row is a SUMMARY of one property, priced at its cheapest nightly rate and not at a total for the stay. The result is one PAGE of the matching set: when more hotels match, the response carries a `Link` header with rel="next" -- follow it, because stopping at the first page answers from a partial list. `limit` and `cursor` are reserved parameter names this verb deliberately does not declare (Section 8.1 item 6); the wire accepts them anyway.

nightly_price_cents.description: EUR cents PER NIGHT for the cheapest room.

output_schema.description: One page of matching hotels. A PAGINATING query declares ONE shape, the same array a non-paginating query declares: whether more hotels match is said by the RFC 8288 `Link` header with rel="next", not by the body (Section 8.4).

queries.name: browse_listings
queries.description: Browse the classifieds board across ALL sellers -- this is the open board, not the caller's own corner of it. The rows carry an owner and this operator publishes them to every principal ON PURPOSE, which is what `reach: published` says; a seller is named by an opaque, stable pseudonym and never by an address.

keyword.description: Case-insensitive match on the listing text.

output_schema.description: Matching listings across all sellers, newest first.

owner_handle.description: The seller's PSEUDONYM on this board -- stable for one account, opaque, and NOT an address.

actions.name: create_order
actions.description: Place an order for what the human has chosen. This RESERVES the goods and returns the order to settle; it does not take money -- the `pay` verb does that.

order_id.description: Name it in the cart mandate, and pass it to any verb that acts on this order.

total_cents.description: EUR cents. Sign the cart at exactly this total.

currency.description: eur -- the currency the cart must be signed in.

output_schema.description: TWO shapes, and the branch is `status`. The pairing is the contract: `setup_required` without a url is an answer an assistant cannot act on.

status.description: A payment method is on file -- proceed to `pay`.
A hosted setup flow must be completed by the human first.

setup_url.description: The hosted page to hand to the human.
